display.title: Havdalah: Why We Smell Besamim When Shabbos Ends
display.summary_short: Why we smell fragrant spices at Havdalah when the extra Shabbos soul departs, and why Shabbos is so precious that keeping it can bring Moshiach.
display.summary_long: A mitzvah-time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, continuing a series on Havdalah. After reviewing the Havdalah kit (wine, cup, spice box and a braided candle with many wicks), Uncle Yossi explains that on Shabbos Hashem gives every Jew an extra soul, the neshamah yeseirah, which makes us daven, learn and behave better. When Shabbos ends it returns to Hashem and we feel a little sad, so we smell the besamim and say the brachah borei minei besamim to lift our spirits. Havdalah opens with words of trust in Hashem, recalling the Baal Shem Tov's father, who told him to fear no one but Hashem. Uncle Yossi then describes the gift of Shabbos: we rest on the day Hashem rested, count the days of the week toward it, save good food and new clothes for it, and if all Jews keep it properly, Moshiach will come.
display.lesson: Shabbos is Hashem's special gift; carry its holiness and trust in Hashem into the whole week.
